statement: There are n boards in a row; boards[i] is the length of board i. You have painters painters, and any painter paints 1 unit of length in 1 unit of time.
Each painter paints one contiguous run of boards, and a board cannot be shared between painters. All painters work at the same time, so the job finishes when the busiest painter does.

Return the minimum time in which all the boards can be painted. The answer lies between max(boards) and the total length; for a candidate time, assigning boards greedily tells you how many painters it needs, so binary search for the smallest time that needs at most painters painters.

examples.explanation: One painter takes [10, 20, 30] (60 units) and the other takes [40]. Any other split leaves one painter with more: [10, 20] / [30, 40] gives 70.
Each of the four painters paints one board, so everything is done in 5 units of time.
